key_insight: AIDE^2 shows that an AI research agent can recursively improve its own code, yielding successive self-optimizations that transfer beyond the tasks used to select them.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path to stronger, more efficient AI research systems by continuously improving the agent that performs the research, not just the model it uses.
method: The system edits its own code and generates candidate rewrites.
Each candidate is benchmarked on AI R&D tasks, and only the best-performing changes are kept using hidden evaluations.
The loop runs autonomously to accumulate successive improvements, including search-policy and memory/context-management updates.
evidence_signal: In an 8-day autonomous run, AIDE^2 found seven successive improvements that generalized to four held-out benchmarks, including out-of-distribution weather forecasting, and reduced reward hacking from 55% to 32% on a separate held-out task family.
watch_item: Because the loop relies on benchmark selection and hidden evaluation, gains may be sensitive to evaluation design and may not fully predict real-world robustness or deployment safety.
paper_title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
